answer: In an agent economy trading pearl and onyx, each bidding identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days, with one active bid allowed per deposit. Creating names is cheap, but running 1,000 identities requires $100,000 locked for a month. Even at the nadir of market activity, that capital stays unavailable. The bond ties bidding capacity to scarce capital, so an attacker must finance every extra identity throughout the lockup.
